name: Depot (GitHub Actions runners)

modes.label: macOS runners (M4 / M2), per minute
modes.note: runner-types docs: $0.08/min. 'Due to licensing constraints from Apple, our macOS runner capacity is not fully elastic' - expect queueing.

modes.label: Windows Server 2025/2022 runners, per minute
modes.note: runner-types docs (2026-09-28): Windows 2 CPU $0.008/min ... 64 CPU $0.256/min (multipliers 2x-64x of the $0.004 base).

modes.label: Depot GitHub Actions runners, Linux x64
modes.note: CI runner. Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). https://depot.dev/docs/github-actions/runner-types: 2 vCPU/8 GB $0.006/min, 4/16 $0.012, 8/32 $0.024, 16/64 $0.048, 32/128 $0.096, 64/256 $0.192. https://depot.dev/pricing: per-second billing, "no one minute minimum"; billed minutes = elapsed x multiplier.

modes.label: Depot GitHub Actions runners, Linux arm64
modes.note: CI runner. Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). https://depot.dev/docs/github-actions/runner-types: arm64 same prices as x64 ($0.006/min per 2 vCPU).

modes.label: Depot Sandboxes (SDK, Depot CI, Managed Agents), per vCPU-second
modes.note: https://depot.dev/pricing (2026-11-08): sandbox compute for Depot CI, Depot Sandboxes and Managed Agents is "$0.00005 / second / vCPU" = $0.18 per vCPU-hour; RAM and disk are not billed separately. Plans include a shared pool of sandbox minutes "measured at 2 vCPUs", so a 4-vCPU sandbox uses 2 included minutes per minute; the pool is not a hard cap. SDK defaults: "2 vCPUs, 4096 MB of memory, and 100 GB of disk"; 2 to 64 vCPUs; max lifetime 24 hours (https://depot.dev/docs/api/sandbox-sdk-reference.md). Isolated Linux microVMs with Docker, x86-64 or ARM64 (https://depot.dev/docs/sandboxes/overview.md). The old $0.01/min agent sandbox rate is no longer listed.

evidence.quote: Depot runners allow outbound connections to any external service

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: 1 user; 2,000 GitHub Actions minutes, 2,000 sandbox minutes (shared by Depot CI, Depot Sandboxes and Managed Agents, measured at 2 vCPUs), 500 container build minutes, 25 GB cache. GHA: billed minutes = elapsed x runner multiplier, overage $0.006/min; 2,000 GHA minutes = $12. Sandbox: overage $0.00005 per vCPU-second; 2,000 minutes at 2 vCPUs = $12. The two pools are separate and each equals $12, so included_usd applies to whichever mode is priced. Source https://depot.dev/pricing (2026-11-08).

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: Unlimited users; 20,000 GitHub Actions minutes, 20,000 sandbox minutes (shared by Depot CI, Depot Sandboxes and Managed Agents, measured at 2 vCPUs), 5,000 container build minutes, 250 GB cache. 20,000 GHA minutes = $120 at $0.006/min; 20,000 sandbox minutes at 2 vCPUs = $120. Separate pools of equal value. Source https://depot.dev/pricing (2026-11-08).

caveats: Included GHA minutes are 'billed minutes' after runner multipliers; the $ value of included minutes for macOS/Windows is unclear, so included_usd is null.
No Hyper-V on Windows runners; macOS capacity not fully elastic.
Included GitHub Actions minutes are billed (multiplied) minutes; encoded as $ at the 2-vCPU rate and applied to Linux modes only (macOS/Windows draw-down not modelled).
2026-09-28 re-check: Linux runners are $0.006/min per 2 vCPU (runner-types + pricing page), not the $0.004/min the audit suggested. Pricing page: unlimited concurrency on every plan.

2026-10-14: nested virtualization (/dev/kvm) exists only on Depot CI sandboxes, not on the GitHub Actions runners priced here (Linux and Windows runner modes carry nested_virt=false). Depot CI itself ("$0.00005 / second / vCPU", 2,000 / 20,000 included Depot CI minutes on Developer / Startup) is not a priced mode on this card.
GitHub Actions runners: the pricing page says per-second billing with no one-minute minimum; billed minutes = elapsed x runner multiplier.

2026-11-08: Depot Sandboxes, Depot CI and Managed Agents share one pool of included sandbox minutes measured at 2 vCPUs, then $0.00005 per vCPU-second. The $0.01/min agent sandbox price is gone. The Sandbox SDK is no longer labeled beta; only detached commands are beta.
2026-11-08: snapshots keep files (home directory and /workspace, up to 25 GiB), not processes. A stopped sandbox cannot restart; restore makes a new sandbox.

fleet.verification: Seven-day trial advertises no credit card.
fleet.notes: Official runner/pricing pages advertise unlimited concurrency. Represent unbounded published plan concurrency as null, not an invented finite maximum; separate anti-abuse/trial capacity guarantees and approval policy are not published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

nested_virt.quote: Nested virtualization is enabled by default on every Depot CI sandbox, with no extra configuration and no extra cost.
nested_virt.note: Depot CI only. The priced GitHub Actions runners have no KVM (https://depot.dev/docs/github-actions/troubleshooting: "Depot GitHub Actions runners don't currently provide /dev/kvm." and "Nested virtualization support is available only in Depot CI sandboxes, where /dev/kvm is enabled by default"), so the linux, linux-arm64 and windows modes override nested_virt to false.

snapshot_auto.note: Managed Agents only: snapshots restore files when a session moves to a new sandbox ("Snapshots preserve files, not running processes"). GHA runners and Sandbox SDK sandboxes save nothing automatically.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Call sandbox.snapshot() while the sandbox is running to save its files.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Sandbox SDK: files from the home directory and /workspace, up to 25 GiB, no memory. Depot CI also has depot/snapshot-action for custom images. Not on the GHA runners.

harness_api.quote: Connect your existing agent provider to Depot Sandboxes without managing runners or workers yourself.
harness_api.note: Managed Agents runs Amp, Claude Code, Claude Managed Agents, Devin and OpenAI agents in Depot sandboxes, started from those tools or the depot claude CLI. No Depot-own prompt/steer/events API is documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Depot's egress filtering system operates at the network layer using iptables on Linux runners. When a runner starts up, our agent process creates a custom iptables chain called `DEPOT_FILTER` in the filter table.
guest_firewall.note: Linux runners are ephemeral single-tenant EC2 VMs with sudo; iptables works (Depot uses it). Windows/macOS runners are also full VMs/hosts (not verified for firewall use).

secret_proxy.quote: Depot puts the real value into request headers sent through its gateway to those hosts, and never into the run.
secret_proxy.note: Managed Agents host-bound secrets ("Send only to hosts"): the sandbox sees only a placeholder. Run secrets, CI secrets, GHA runners and the Sandbox SDK still pass secrets as environment variables.

volume_attach.quote: Mount a durable disk into your Depot CI jobs to persist data between runs and share a directory across multiple workflows.
volume_attach.note: Depot CI cache disks (beta, free during beta), mounted with the depot/cache-mount action under an org-global name. Not documented for the GHA runners product (which has the Depot Cache service instead).

volume_shared.quote: Multiple parallel workflows can mount, read from, and write to the same disk at once.
volume_shared.note: Read-write concurrent across jobs/repos in the org (Depot CI only, beta); docs recommend one writer / partitioned directories.

isolation.quote: Each GitHub Actions job runs on a new EC2 instance that has never been used before, ensuring complete isolation at the hardware level.
isolation.note: GHA runners: a new EC2 instance per job. Depot CI, Depot Sandboxes and Managed Agents run in "isolated Linux microVMs for running code, tests, and agents" (https://depot.dev/docs/sandboxes/overview.md).

image_oci.quote: Standard container images can't boot, even if pushed to Depot Registry.
image_oci.note: Custom images must be Depot snapshot images in Depot Registry; public registries are not supported. GHA runner custom images are AMIs (Business plan).

anti_bot.quote: Depot is a build infrastructure platform offering: (1) Depot container builds ... (2) Depot GitHub Actions runners ... (6) Depot Managed ... and (7) Depot agent sandboxes - secure cloud sandboxes for AI coding tools.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (CI/build infrastructure and coding-agent sandboxes, not browser automation/scraping).

captcha_solving.quote: Depot is a build infrastructure platform offering: (1) Depot container builds ... (2) Depot GitHub Actions runners ... (6) Depot Managed ... and (7) Depot agent sandboxes - secure cloud sandboxes for AI coding tools.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: By default, each Depot runner launches with a unique public IP address from the AWS (Amazon Web Services) address pool.

wake_on_request.quote: GitHub Actions runners launch on-demand in response to webhook events from your organization.
wake_on_request.note: Sandboxes start only by an explicit Sandbox.create (or a Managed Agents session); no wake on an incoming request.

live_resize.quote: resources: the compute to request, as {vcpus?, memoryMb?, diskGb?} ... Sandboxes support 2 to 64 vCPUs.
live_resize.note: Resources are fixed at sandbox creation; only `setTimeout` (lifetime extension) is documented for a running sandbox, no API to change vCPU/RAM of a running machine.

own_agent_api.quote: Connect your existing agent provider to Depot Sandboxes without managing runners or workers yourself.
own_agent_api.note: Managed Agents hosts third-party agents (modeled as harness_api); Depot ships no first-party agent of its own.

mcp_server.quote: Depot skills give AI coding agents the product context they need to use Depot from a shell. ... The key is `depot ci run`
mcp_server.note: Depot's documented agent-facing surfaces are a CLI, REST/protobuf API, and an installable 'skills' package (github.com/depot/skills); no MCP server is documented on depot.dev or listed among the depot GitHub org's public repos (checked via GitHub API).

lang_python.quote: Agent sandboxes come pre-installed with popular programming languages, package managers, and development tools.
lang_python.note: Not itemized by name, but 'popular programming languages' for a coding-agent sandbox implies Python/Node; GHA runner labels (e.g. depot-ubuntu-24.04) are a drop-in replacement mirroring GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner images, which ship Python by default.

lang_node.quote: Agent sandboxes come pre-installed with popular programming languages, package managers, and development tools.
lang_node.note: Same reasoning as lang_python; Claude Code itself (the harness Depot runs) is a Node.js CLI, and GHA runner images mirror GitHub-hosted images which ship Node.js by default.

ingress_rules.quote: Depot GitHub Actions runners are a drop-in replacement for your existing runners in any GitHub Actions job.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Depot's runners/sandboxes don't expose inbound ports/URLs for external traffic (card already has public_ipv4 and inbound_https as false), so there is nothing to apply per-request ingress access control to.

egress_http_rules.quote: You can add more rules to allow or deny connections to specific IPs, CIDRs, or hostnames.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress filtering operates at the network layer (iptables, by IP/CIDR/hostname); no HTTP method/path-level egress rules are documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: All runners either peer with your AWS account or are configured to use a NAT gateway for static outbound IP addresses. These IPs can then be allowlisted in your firewall or security policies.
static_egress_ip.note: Only via a Business-plan custom/dedicated deployment; the default runner fleet uses per-job dynamic AWS IPs (network.ipv4_available is false for the default product).

soc2.note: Type II. The Type I post (https://depot.dev/blog/depot-soc-2) dates from March 2024.

max_session_h.quote: The maximum sandbox lifetime is 24 hours.
max_session_h.note: Sandbox SDK. Managed Agents continue a session in a new sandbox from the latest workspace snapshot. GHA runner jobs have no documented cap here.

snapshot.quote: Snapshots preserve files, not running processes or memory.
snapshot.note: Sandbox SDK snapshot() (up to 25 GiB) and Depot CI snapshot-action; filesystem only, so fs not mem.

volumes.quote: Mount a durable disk into your Depot CI jobs to persist data between runs and share a directory across multiple workflows. ... Multiple parallel workflows can mount, read from, and write to the same disk at once.
volumes.note: Contradiction confirmed: card said volumes=false while volume_attach/volume_shared were already true in feature_evidence for the same Depot CI cache-disks beta feature (durable attach + shared mount).

pause_resume.quote: sandbox.stop stops the sandbox gracefully. The sandbox ends in the finished status. ... sandbox.kill cancels the sandbox immediately. The sandbox ends in the cancelled status.
pause_resume.note: No pause or resume. A stopped sandbox ends in the finished status and cannot restart; continue by snapshot + Sandbox.create (see persist_scope).

fork.quote: Pass the returned snapshot (or its snapshotId) to Sandbox.create, which restores the files into a new sandbox.
fork.how: snapshot a running sandbox and create several new sandboxes from that snapshot; files only, no live processes or memory
fork.note: No fork or clone call; a file-level copy through snapshot + create.

fork_running.quote: Sandbox.create provisions a new sandbox. Every option is optional; the server fills in defaults for anything you leave unset.
fork_running.note: No live fork. snapshot() keeps files only ("Snapshots preserve files, not running processes or memory"), so a running machine with its processes cannot be cloned. A file-level copy works: see fork.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Snapshots preserve files, not running processes or memory.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Depot's only snapshot mechanism explicitly excludes running process/memory state, and there is no fork feature to combine it with.

ssh.quote: Direct SSH connects you to the Depot sandbox environment over exec.depot.dev using your Depot API token. This gives you a shell on the sandbox... Use depot ci ssh <run-id> --job <job> to connect to a job that's already in progress.
ssh.note: Depot CI jobs support direct interactive SSH access (and a tmate-based flow) into the running sandbox. Card wrongly had ssh=false.

desktop.quote: Depot accelerates your CI, container builds, and GitHub Actions.
desktop.note: Product is CI/build/agent-sandbox compute (Linux/Windows/macOS runners, sandboxes); no graphical desktop/VNC/RDP offering is documented anywhere in the docs.

computer_use.quote: Depot accelerates your CI, container builds, and GitHub Actions.
computer_use.note: No screenshot/click-driving API exists; product is CI runners, container builds, and coding-agent sandboxes, not a browser/desktop-automation product.

inbound_https.quote: networkUsage: bytes sent and received, as {ingressBytes, egressBytes}.
inbound_https.note: No documented way to expose an inbound URL or port on a sandbox or runner. Private access goes the other way, through Tailscale.

public_ipv4.quote: Configure egress filtering to control which external services your GitHub Actions runners can connect to by blocking or allowing connections at the network level.
public_ipv4.note: Docs describe outbound network control (egress allowlists, Tailscale) only; no mention of a per-machine public inbound IPv4 address.

agent_harnesses.quote: Connect your existing agent provider to Depot Sandboxes without managing runners or workers yourself.
agent_harnesses.note: Providers listed: Amp, Claude Code, Claude Managed Agents, Devin, OpenAI.

gpu.quote: Depot Managed allows you to leverage your own GPU resources on AWS to accelerate AI/ML and GPU-intensive GitHub Actions workflows. ... the Depot team will build and deploy a custom AMI to your Depot Managed environment.
gpu.note: GPU runner support exists, but only for Depot Managed (Business plan, deployed into the customer's own AWS account) with a custom GPU AMI built on request — not a self-serve GPU size on the standard GHA runner catalog priced on the card.

self_host.quote: Depot Managed is still a fully managed service and comes with the full support and SLA of the Depot Business plan. The Depot team is on-call for any issues that arise with the Depot Managed deployment.
self_host.note: Even Depot's 'run in your own AWS account' offering (Depot Managed / byoc) remains operated by Depot; there is no mode where the customer runs the Depot software themselves.

open_source.quote: We have made all of our documentation open source so that you can contribute to it if you'd like... it's available at depot/docs on GitHub.
open_source.note: Only the documentation (and the thin @depot/sandbox client SDK) is open source; the core CI/runner/sandbox platform itself has no published OSI license and is a commercial managed/BYOC service.

eu_data_residency.quote: Today, Depot operates cloud infrastructure in regions that are geographically located inside the United States of America as well as the European Union (if a project chooses the EU as its region).
eu_data_residency.note: Per-project EU region selection is documented, matching the card's own regions: ["us","eu"]. Card wrongly had eu_data_residency=false.

private_network.quote: By connecting Depot to your Tailscale network, you can enable secure access to private services, such as databases, within your tailnet without opening up those services to the public internet... Depot GitHub Actions runners, container builders, and CI jobs join your tailnet as ephemeral nodes.
private_network.note: Tailscale: GHA runners, container builders, CI jobs, and also Depot Sandboxes and Managed Agents sandboxes ("Agent sandboxes automatically join your organization's Tailscale tailnet", https://depot.dev/docs/managed-agents/overview). Not on Windows runners.

usage_api.quote: sandbox SDK only reports networkUsage {ingressBytes, egressBytes}; no billable usage, cost, or per-sandbox metrics endpoint documented. Pricing is per-minute (runners) or per-second (Depot CI), billed via dashboard/invoice only.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Extensive feature documentation and 2026-09-30 audit found no programmatic usage API for individual sandboxes or projects. Monitoring is byte-level only; billing is account/invoice level.

persist_scope.quote: Call sandbox.snapshot() while the sandbox is running to save its files. ... Pass the returned snapshot (or its snapshotId) to Sandbox.create, which restores the files into a new sandbox.
persist_scope.how: call sandbox.snapshot() before the sandbox ends, then pass the snapshot to Sandbox.create; files in the home directory and /workspace come back (up to 25 GiB), not processes or memory. Managed Agents do this automatically.
persist_scope.note: A stopped sandbox cannot restart; a restore always makes a new sandbox, and changes after the last snapshot are lost. GHA runners are never reused. Sandboxes with repository- or environment-scoped secrets cannot be snapshotted (https://depot.dev/docs/sandboxes/overview.md).

credential_injection.quote: Depot puts the real value into request headers sent through its gateway to those hosts, and never into the run.

locations_quote: For Depot-hosted projects, you can select between our US East and EU Central regions. This feature allows you to launch your image builders in the region closest to your registry by selecting your desired region when creating a new project.

audit_2026_11_08.source: findings/depot.json checked against depot.dev pricing, Sandbox SDK reference, Sandboxes overview, Managed Agents overview and security pages
